question: A coordinator needs to orchestrate a large-scale codebase migration involving on the order of two hundred independent file-level subtasks, far more than the handful of subagents a coordinator typically delegates to per turn. Which approach is best suited to this scale?
options: A) Split the migration across multiple coordinators that each independently maintain their own separate pipeline
B) Invoke a single general-purpose subagent and have it sequentially handle all subtasks within one context window
C) Keep using turn-by-turn subagent delegation but increase the coordinator's maxTurns to accommodate more invocations
D) Use the Workflow tool to move orchestration into a script the runtime executes outside the conversation itself
correct_answers: D) Use the Workflow tool to move orchestration into a script the runtime executes outside the conversation itself
explanations: Multiple independent coordinators with no shared state would duplicate effort and lose the centralized tracking needed to know which of two hundred subtasks are complete.
A single subagent handling two hundred subtasks sequentially in one context window loses the parallelism and context-isolation benefits, and risks exhausting that context window.
Raising maxTurns lets a single agent take more turns, but turn-by-turn subagent delegation is still designed for a handful of subagents per turn, not hundreds of coordinated subtasks.

Correct. For runs coordinating dozens to hundreds of agents, the Workflow tool moves orchestration into a script the runtime executes outside the conversation, which fits this scale better than turn-by-turn delegation.
